title: Care work — the basics
_note: English for work (english-for-work run, 2026-11-02): written by hand in British English, not yet checked by a second reader. translations.en = short definition in simple English; deHint = German translation (the 'German' tab). Words that already exist in the English lexicon are refs with a job-specific example.
intro: A short first deck for care work: the people, places and everyday tasks in a care home or hospital, and a few kind phrases to say to residents and patients. Every word has an example sentence from a real working day in the UK.
introEasy: Do you work in a care home or hospital? Learn your first words for care work here.
tipps: Speak slowly and kindly. Say your name and what you are going to do: “Hello Mr Hughes, I'm Amira. I'm going to help you wash.”
Always ask before you touch someone: “Is it OK if I help you up?” Then wait for the answer.
If you are not sure about something, ask a senior colleague or the nurse. Never guess with medication or health.

words.example: Some of our residents have dementia.

words.example: I'll help you wash and then we'll have breakfast.
